notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card names the PythonObjectDriver helper; the package uses a direct Driver over xia_pfcu.pfcu:PFCU because the upstream commands are !PFCU<module> <command> frames and the replies are multi-line status/enum decodes, and because the class has a sync/async protocol split. The fake is the package stand-in: the upstream simulator is a sinstruments BaseDevice whose entry point is handle_message, not the PFCU object the driver calls, and it needs gevent/sinstruments, which the gate must not install. The only gate warning is G4.REF_VALUE on the decimation upper bound: xia_pfcu/protocol.py:94 states 65_535 as a Python literal and the gate's number reader splits it into 65 and 535; the clone has no plain 65535 text and the PDF is not cited. Risk is R2 because cap.optics.shutter.v1 is R2 and the shutter is an optical-path actuator; the safe-state action x-cap.tiagocoutinho.close_shutter.v1 and the @estop both call the native close_shutter. The shutter commands only work when shutter mode is enabled, and the driver exposes that mode as a writable boolean. The exposure duration is operator_required; site-limits.example.json is only an example overlay (0.01 to 3600 s), not a device fact. The fake starts with shutter mode enabled and the shutter closed (placeholders) so the paths are testable; the upstream power-up default is disabled. Model-authored and unreviewed: the R2 hardware backend is refused by the loader until reviewed_by is set in driver.lock.json. NOT COVERED: insert_filter, remove_filter and clear_short_error (the four set_filters fields cover the filter channels; a latched short is not retried), the per-channel shorted/open/TTL/front-panel details, and the raw write_readline command. The hardware backend (native.py, a connio connection) was never run, and the fake is an in-memory stand-in, not a recording.
